summary: A text input that filters a list of options as the user types, then selects one or several of them. Built for long lists and async search (people, repositories, tokens).
whenToUse: Choosing from a long or growing list where typing is faster than scrolling: reviewers, repositories, components, tokens.
Results come from a server: control inputValue, fetch, pass the results as options with filter={null} and loading while waiting.
Several values from a long list (multiple): selected values become removable chips inside the field.
whenNotToUse: Short known lists (under about ten): use Select, which needs no typing.
Free text with suggestions (a search box): the value must be one of the options here, so use Input or an autocomplete pattern.
Two or three options: use RadioGroup.

dos.title: Add a second line when names are ambiguous
dos.text: A role or an email under the name helps pick the right Ada, and is matched by screen readers too.

dos.title: Write an empty message that says what to try
dos.text: "No one matches. Check the spelling or invite them." turns a dead end into a next step.

p.label: Reviewer
p.emptyMessage: No one matches. Check the spelling or invite them.

donts.title: Spinner with no words
donts.text: While loading, say what is happening ("Searching people"). The message is also announced to screen readers.

donts.title: Combobox for a handful of fixed options
donts.text: Typing to find one of three themes is slower than seeing them. Use Select or RadioGroup.

accessibility: Base UI Combobox: the input has role combobox with aria-expanded, aria-controls and aria-activedescendant; the popup is a listbox.

Keyboard: typing filters; Down Arrow opens and moves; Enter selects; Escape closes, then clears; with multiple, Left Arrow from the start of the input moves through the chips and Backspace removes one.
loading renders the message in a live status region and sets aria-busy on the popup; the empty message is announced the same way.
The clear and toggle buttons inside the field have accessible names ("Clear selection", "Show options"); each chip remove button says "Remove <name>".
The Field label names the input; hint and error are linked through aria-describedby.
The popup is portaled and re-applies the theme, brand and density of its field.
contentGuidelines: Placeholder hints at what to type: "Search people", "Type a component name".
Empty message: say there is no match and what to try next, in one sentence.
Loading message is a present participle phrase: "Searching people", "Loading repositories".
Option labels are the names users know (people's display names, component names), not ids.

anatomy.control: Field box holding prefix, chips, input and actions
